name: Stairs and baby gates

0-3m.rationale: Not mobile yet; the main risk is a fall while being carried on stairs.

3-6m.rationale: Still carried everywhere; one study found about a quarter of under-1 stair injuries happened while being carried.

6-12m.rationale: Crawling and pulling up begin; the same study found infants hurt on stairs were over 3 times as likely to be hospitalized.

12-24m.rationale: New walkers and climbers; the study counted over 93,000 stair injuries in children under 5 over 10 years.

24-36m.rationale: Climbing is confident but balance and judgment are still developing; the evidence is not split by age so this is scored conservatively.

36-60m.rationale: Stairs are usually managed with supervision; evidence is not split by age, so this is scored conservatively.

injury_evidence.note: Nationwide Children's Hospital news release (Mar 12, 2012) on a Pediatrics study using CPSC NEISS data: more than 93,000 children under 5 treated in U.S. emergency departments for stair injuries from 1999 to 2008, about one every six minutes on average; one-fourth of injuries in infants under 1 happened while being carried on stairs. Verify against the Pediatrics article itself (the full paper was not opened).

why_it_matters: Babies can be hurt on stairs while being carried, and crawlers and new walkers can tumble down them in seconds. A properly installed gate at the top and bottom reduces the risk.

fix_steps.text: Until a gate is up, keep the child off the stairs, hold their hand when they climb or descend, and keep stairs clear of clutter.
Install a gate at the bottom of the stairs, and a gate that screws into the wall at the top (not a pressure-fit or pet gate).
Skip accordion-style and older V-shaped-opening gates; they can trap an arm, head or neck.
Keep stairs well lit and carry a baby with one hand free to hold the rail.

reminder.text: Check that stair gates are still firmly latched and the wall mounts have not loosened.

verify_rule: A gate is fixed with screws at the top of every stairway the child can reach, latches closed, and does not move when pushed firmly.
blind_spots: Whether a gate is screwed into a stud or only a pressure fit
Stairs in other parts of the house or at relatives' homes
